text.p: These are the leading stories in the Belgrade press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified them and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- The U.N. Security council lifts Yugoslav sanctions after four years and four months. "Today, we have all finally come out together of the most difficult period of our counry's modern history" said Serbian President Slobodan MIlosevic in a special statement.
- The lifting of sanctions against Yugoslavia is an extremely important event, says federal foreign minister Milan Milutinovic.
- The U.N. Transitional Administration in Eastern Slavonia (UNTAES) will decide when elections will be organised in the region, says spokesman Philip Arnold.
- Serbian power industry EPS has introduced higher tariffs above a set consumption quota which will mostly affect the big electricity consumers.

- Increase of trade deficit could jeopardise stability of the dinar so additional measures for promoting export and reducing public expenditure are needed, says the finance committee of the Yugoslav chamber of economy.
- Resumption of Yugoslav Airlines flights to the U.S. and Canada will depend on the profitability of the venture, says director Zika Petrovic.
- There will be more foreign goods on the Serbian market after barriers are lifted, says Serbian Deputy Prime Minister Slobodan Radulovic.
- Opposition coalition Zajedno resolves differences over distribution of mandates and is ready to submit election lists.
- Milk producers will have to return prices to earlier levels because Serbian trade ministry did not authorise the rise.
- President of the Serb regional government in Eastern Slavonia Vojislav Stanimirovic says elections in the area cannot be organised before the spring.
- UNTAES launched campaign to buy personal weapons from residents of the Eastern Slavonia to get small arms out of houses and off the streets. The action is financed by the Croatian government.
- Yugoslav Prime Minister Radoje Kontic is visiting Slovakia on October 3, and 4.

- Transport agreement between Yugoslavia and Macedonia will start on October 4 and the two sides agreed to continue promoting cooperation, says Yugoslav transport and communications minister Zoran Vujovic after talks with visiting Macedonian delegation.
